questions.questionText: Extract B (line 19) states: ‘In Nigeria, the demand for rice is very price inelastic’. With the help of a diagram, explain how the Indian export ban is likely to have affected the market for rice in Nigeria.

Table 2 shows the weekly demand for two products, apples and pears, before and after a change in the price of pears. What is the cross elasticity of demand for apples following the change in the price of pears?
Which one of the following is most likely to indicate that a government is trying to cause a significant change in the pattern of economic activity?
options: A reduction in the rate of tax on income from retirement pensions
A reduction in the tax on a good with positive consumption externalities
An increase in the rate of an inheritance tax
An increase in the tax on a good with very inelastic demand

questions.questionText: The cross elasticity of demand for Good R is –0.5 with respect to the price of Good S. If the price of Good S falls by 20%, demand for Good R will
options: fall by 10%.
fall by 40%.
rise by 10%.
rise by 40%.

questions.questionText: Figure 3 shows a firm’s demand curve (D). If the firm raises its price from £3 to £5, demand is
options: price elastic and total revenue will fall.
price elastic and total revenue will rise.
price inelastic and total revenue will fall.
price inelastic and total revenue will rise.

questions.questionText: A household's annual income increases from £35 000 to £38 500. All other things being equal, if the household's income elasticity of demand for Good X is –0.2 and its income elasticity of demand for Good Y is 0.4, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Spending on Good X will fall by £70 and spending on Good Y will increase by £140
Spending on Good X will fall by £700 and spending on Good Y will increase by £1400
Spending on Good X will fall by 2% and spending on Good Y will increase by 4%
Spending on Good X will fall by 20% and spending on Good Y will increase by 40%

questions.questionText: According to the kinked demand curve model of oligopoly, which one of the following would be most likely to explain price stability in an oligopolistic market?
options: A firm's revenue would fall with any change in price
Collusion between firms is likely to lead to price-fixing
Firms do not seek to maximise their profits
Individual firms do not have the ability to set prices

questions.questionText: A bakery decides to increase the price of the bread that it sells. Which one of the following price elasticities of demand for bread will result in the largest increase in the bakery’s total revenue?

A government sets a maximum price for fruit below the market price to try to encourage healthier eating. All other things being equal, which one of the following will result in the lowest amount of excess demand for fruit at the maximum price?
options: Demand is income elastic and supply is price elastic.
Demand is income inelastic and supply is price inelastic.
Demand is price elastic and supply is price elastic.
Demand is price inelastic and supply is price inelastic.

questions.questionText: The income elasticity of demand for cheese sandwiches is –1.2. This means that cheese sandwiches
options: are a normal good.
are an inferior good.
have an income inelastic demand.
have many substitutes.

questions.questionText: Table 1 shows the price of a packet of peanuts and the number of packets of cashew nuts sold in a shop in one month. The price of a packet of cashew nuts is unchanged. When the price of a packet of peanuts rises from £0.80 to £0.84, the cross elasticity of demand for cashew nuts with respect to the price of peanuts is
A government decides to increase its subsidy to rail services to encourage more people to travel by rail. The subsidy is most likely to be successful if rail travel has a
options: demand that is elastic with respect to price.
demand that is inelastic with respect to price.
high positive income elasticity of demand.
negative cross elasticity of demand with respect to car travel.

questions.questionText: The cross elasticity of demand for chips with respect to the price of rice is positive. It can be concluded that chips and rice are
options: inferior goods.
jointly demanded.
normal goods.
substitute goods.

questions.questionText: Figure 3 shows the demand curve for a firm’s scarves. Which one of the following statements is true when the price of scarves is reduced from £30 to £25?
options: Demand for scarves is price elastic.
Price elasticity of demand is –0.5.
The firm’s total revenue falls.
The firm’s total revenue increases.

questions.questionText: Explain how the concept of cross elasticity of demand can be used to understand the relationship between markets.

A monopolistically competitive firm’s demand curve for good X has a price elasticity of demand of minus 1.0 throughout its entire range. All other things being equal, which one of the following is most likely to result in an increase in the firm’s profits?
options: A decrease in the cost of producing the good
A decrease in the price of the good
An increase in the price of the good
An increase in the scale of its operation

questions.questionText: Figure 4 shows a firm’s demand (D) curve and its marginal revenue (MR) curve for good X. The firm initially sells OQ1 units of X per day at a price of OP1. If the firm increases its price by 10%
options: price elasticity of demand will decrease.
price elasticity of demand will not change.
total revenue will decrease.
total revenue will increase.

questions.questionText: Table 1 shows the prices and quantities of rice and pasta sold in a supermarket in one month. When the price of rice rises from £2.00 to £2.25, the cross elasticity of demand for pasta with respect to the price of rice is
A firm producing frozen foods has collected statistics on recent trends in sales of oven chips, as shown in Table 3. These statistics suggest that oven chips
options: are a normal good.
are an inferior good.
have an income elasticity of demand greater than 1.
have an income elasticity of demand less than 0.

questions.questionText: A clothes retailer has experimented with changing the prices of various items of clothing sold in their shop. The table below shows the different prices per item in 2 years. Other things being equal, which one of the following changes from Year 1 to Year 2 is the retailer most likely to experience?
options: A decrease in revenue from socks if the price elasticity of demand is minus one
A decrease in revenue from T-shirts if the price elasticity of demand is elastic
An increase in revenue from trainers if the price elasticity of demand is inelastic
An increase in revenue from trousers if the price elasticity of demand is elastic

questions.questionText: Explain how the impact of a minimum price for a good or service is affected by its price elasticity of demand and its price elasticity of supply.

A pizza takeaway raises the price of its pizzas by 5%, resulting in a 10% fall in demand for their pizzas. Also, the next-door fish and chip shop sees the demand for its food rise by 10%. Which one of the following combinations of elasticities represents these events?

The diagram below shows the market demand (D) curve and two supply (S1 and S2) curves for a brand of soft drink. The drink is a demerit good because of its high sugar content. The government imposes an indirect tax on each can sold that cuts consumption by 100 000 cans per week. If the price elasticity of demand for the drink is –2.0, the price must have increased by
options: 5p

questions.questionText: The price elasticity of demand (PED) for petrol used by car drivers in an economy is estimated to be –0.2. Which one of the following is the most likely reason for the low PED?
options: A tax on petrol
Cycle lanes on many roads
Few bus and rail services
Low household incomes

questions.questionText: The income elasticity of demand for baked beans is –0.4. Weekly sales of baked beans are 73 000 tins. If household incomes fall by 5%, then the new weekly sales of baked bean tins would be
There is a large increase in the number of different models of bicycles produced by the bicycle industry. The most likely impact of this would be
options: a decrease in advertising expenditure by bicycle firms.
a fall in the price elasticity of demand for any one model of bicycle.
an increase in barriers to entry to the bicycle industry.
an increase in productivity of manufacturing bicycles.

questions.questionText: The price of good Y, a substitute for good X, rises from 75p to £1. As a result, the quantity of demand for good X rises from 3 million units to 5 million units per month. What is the value of the cross elasticity of demand for good X with respect to good Y?

At the initial market equilibrium, the income elasticity of demand for fresh chickens is +1.5, and the price elasticity of supply is +1.0. Then there is a 5% increase in consumers’ income. Which one of the following combinations, A, B, C or D, is most likely to show the changes in the market equilibrium price and quantity?
Which one of the following gives a positive value for the cross elasticity of demand?
options: A fall in air fares increases the demand for holidays
A fall in the cost of car insurance increases the demand for cars
A rise in the price of petrol decreases the demand for cars
A rise in rail fares increases the demand for coach travel

questions.questionText: A supermarket has estimated values of the income elasticity of demand for some of its products as shown in the table below. If incomes increase by 5%, for which of these grocery items will the quantity demanded increase by more than 1%?
options: Eggs
Fruit
Fruit and cheese
Milk and eggs

questions.questionText: If firms in an industry increase their spending on advertising, it is likely to
options: help firms to differentiate their products.
make it easier for new firms to enter the industry.
make the demand for the firms’ products more elastic.
reduce the monopoly power of the firms in the industry.

questions.questionText: The price elasticity of demand for games consoles is -1.2. It can be concluded that a 10% reduction in their price would lead to a percentage change in demand of
The cross elasticity of demand between goods X and Y is positive. This implies that they are
options: normal goods.
substitute goods.
goods in composite demand.
complementary goods.
